conventions.convention: Assume countable choice and supply chosen tubular and peripheral data; the longitude has degree +1 over the knot and zero exterior homology. The meridian–longitude basis is explicitly assumed.

The exterior boundary has μ·λ = −1. A slope is unoriented: (p,q) and (−p,−q) agree. Filling uses an orientation-reversing boundary gluing with meridian image pμ+qλ and retains the exterior orientation; integer n means nμ+λ.
For coprime p>0 and q, L(p,q) is the oriented filling E_U(p/q). No symbol L(0,q) is assigned.
The trace is a single smooth 2-handle attachment only for integer framing n, with attaching parallel nμ+λ and orientation-compatible attachment.

The trefoil is the closure of the positive geometric braid σ₁³. In ambient coordinates (x,y,t), the viewing normal is +y, the projection basis is (∂t,∂x), and each right-starting branch passes over. The based positive meridian is a and λ=(ab)³a⁻⁶.
The counterexample's permutations act on {1,2,3,4,5} with rightmost factor applied first.

load_bearing.statement: For a slope represented by p[μ]+q[λ], the Dehn filling E_K(p/q) glues an oriented solid torus by an orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphism sending its meridian to that slope; the filled orientation agrees with E_K. Its oriented homeomorphism type is independent of the gluing map once the meridian image is fixed.

Assume ACω. For a smooth oriented knot with chosen connected exterior, positive meridian, preferred degree-one null-homologous longitude forming a boundary homology basis, and coprime integers p,q not both zero, H₁(E_K(p/q);Z) is Z/|p|Z when p≠0 and Z when p=0.

Assume ACω. For the specified positive geometric trefoil and based positive meridian a, π₁(E_T(1/1)) ≅ ⟨a,b | aba=bab, bab⁻¹aba⁻²=1⟩. The blackboard parallel is w=bac with c=b⁻¹ab, wa³=(ab)³, and λ=wa⁻³=(ab)³a⁻⁶; equivalently the filling relation is (ab)³=a⁵.

Assume ACω. Attach one orientation-compatible smooth 2-handle to B⁴ along a smooth oriented knot K with product framing whose parallel has slope n[μ]+[λ], n∈Z. After rounding corners, the oriented boundary of X_n(K) is E_K(n/1).
For coprime integers p>0 and q, L(p,q) denotes the oriented union of the unknot exterior and a solid torus whose meridian is identified with p[μ_U]+q[λ_U]; thus L(p,q)=E_U(p/q).

H₁(T²)=Z² with the factor-circle basis, as established in its verification.
Replacing collar-thickened pieces by the exterior, solid torus, and boundary torus.
Injectivity of the Mayer–Vietoris H₀ map for connected pieces and overlap.
The two-strand base configuration, endpoint permutation, and transported strand labels.
The explicit positive diamond motion and the identity of the overpassing strand.
Stacking three positive half twists with the prescribed endpoint relabeling.
The fixed closure map, increasing-parameter orientation, and identification of corresponding endpoint positions.
Regular projection and over/under conventions underlying the trefoil diagram.
Filling adds the normal relation killing the attaching meridian slope; no injectivity of peripheral maps is required.
Identifying trefoil exterior first homology with the abelianization of its Wirtinger presentation.
